notes: Run this benchmark from the slopsentral checkout after materializing the Kotlin Engineering best-practices package.
The default workspace.sourcePath assumes a sibling Kotlin repository; teams should replace it with their own Kotlin/Gradle repository path before collecting baseline usage.

The repository-guidance scenario is a portable rewrite of the current Kast AGENTS.md observed on 2026-08-23; it excludes Kast-specific module counts, platform versions, documentation tooling, and exact commands.
Feed the resulting benchmark-usage.jsonl back into plugin-eval analyze with --observed-usage before treating static budget warnings as production blockers.
Astra-targeted definition; static validation and golden replay are not a live model benchmark result.
setupQuestions: Which Kotlin/Gradle repository should represent the daily-driver team workflow?
Which scenario must pass before Kotlin Engineering is promoted to a team default?
Which focused Gradle task proves each scenario without hiding failures behind a broad aggregate build?
What token and retry budget is acceptable for a successful Kotlin Engineering run?

scenarios.title: Kotlin invariant semantic evidence
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether the Kotlin Engineering package changes the implementation path for a type-safety task instead of allowing stringly edits plus broad validation.
scenarios.userInput: Use Kotlin Engineering for this Kotlin repository. Change a Kotlin API so an invalid raw string state is no longer representable, find all callers safely, and prove the owning Gradle tests still pass. Do not commit, push, publish, open or update a pull request, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The run records Kast semantic evidence for affected Kotlin symbols.
The implementation moves the invariant into Kotlin types rather than comments, nullable flags, or caller discipline.
The final answer includes the focused successful Gradle command.

scenarios.title: Gradle failure structured reports
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether the Kotlin Engineering package diagnoses a failed Kotlin test from structured reports and keeps the rerun narrow.
scenarios.userInput: Use Kotlin Engineering for this Kotlin repository. A Kotlin test fails in Gradle; diagnose the failure, fix it, and rerun the smallest useful Gradle task before saying it is green. Do not commit, push, publish, open or update a pull request, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The run records kotlin-gradle-validation runner JSON or parser JSON when the bundled scripts are available.
The diagnosis cites JUnit XML, Gradle problem reports, Kotlin build reports, or explicitly records that they were absent.
The fix is grounded in the failing test behavior, not only the first console line.
The final answer includes the smallest successful relevant Gradle command.

scenarios.title: Negative capability before and after
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether advanced Kotlin type-safety work proves a previously reachable misuse and removes it from the API surface.
scenarios.userInput: Use Kotlin Engineering for this Kotlin repository. Prove that an invalid Kotlin operation used to be representable, then refactor the API so the same misuse no longer compiles. Do not commit, push, publish, open or update a pull request, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The run records a negative-capability proof JSON path or explains why the helper was unavailable.
The run records a before-state misuse or representable invalid state.
The fix moves enforcement into Kotlin types, constructors, or sealed APIs.
The after-state proof shows the misuse no longer compiles or is no longer constructible.

scenarios.title: Kotlin repository task and topology proof
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether Kotlin Engineering preserves task, refinement, module, instruction, consumer, and installed-artifact evidence across a multi-module behavior change.
scenarios.userInput: Use Kotlin Engineering to implement this multi-module behavior change. Preserve each validated Kotlin value as a stronger type across callers, keep concrete adapters out of pure module APIs, maintain only the AGENTS.md files whose durable facts changed, and leave fresh executable red and green task proof. Widen verification through the owning module, affected consumers, generated boundaries, and installed public artifact only where the changed contract requires it. Do not commit, push, publish, open or update a pull request, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: The numbered task has five definition files and kotlin_task_evidence check accepts current red and green proof outputs.
Changed validation APIs document and return stronger types or closed typed failures, and callers consume those results.
Pure modules expose domain-owned contracts while one minimal integration module selects concrete adapters.
A mechanical dependency or public-API check rejects implementation leakage.
Root topology and nearest local AGENTS.md guidance agree with Gradle membership and changed ownership without duplicated parent rules.
Verification records only the affected focused, owner, consumer, generated-boundary, and installed-artifact rings.

scenarios.title: Kotlin application stack private bindings
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether Kotlin Engineering uses the preferred application libraries without exposing their implementation types through domain modules or imposing native-image delivery without evidence.
scenarios.userInput: Use Kotlin Engineering to build this Kotlin CLI and HTTP client. Use Clikt command families with sensible defaults and shell completion, Ktor Client, and kotlinx.serialization. Keep domain modules pure, select concrete bindings in one small integration module, add public CLI and adapter tests, and adopt GraalVM native-image delivery only if a feasibility check supports it. Do not commit, push, publish, open or update a pull request, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: Public domain signatures do not expose Clikt, Ktor, serialization, engine, or native-image types.
A focused adapter implements a domain-owned capability and one integration module selects it.
A mechanical dependency or public-API check rejects implementation leakage into pure modules.
Clikt tests cover help, defaults, completion, one successful command, and one rejected invocation.
Ktor client tests use MockEngine and serialized fixtures without live network access.
The native-image choice records compatibility and measurable delivery criteria instead of applying a universal rule.

scenarios.title: Kotlin delivery companion boundary
scenarios.purpose: Measure whether end-to-end Kotlin delivery composes the Kotlin Engineering best-practices package with Git/CI Operations without absorbing generic branch and PR ownership.
scenarios.userInput: Use the Kotlin repository default workflow. Prepare a Kotlin type-safety change, validate it with Gradle, and audit the local delivery handoff. Do not commit, push, open or update a pull request, monitor CI, or otherwise modify remote state.
successChecklist: Kotlin proof includes semantic or Gradle evidence from Kotlin Engineering.
The local delivery audit covers scoped staging and identifies the later commit, PR, and CI evidence without performing those actions.
The run does not move generic Git, PR, CI, or release instructions into Kotlin Engineering.
